title: Hnrnph2 loss couples Rsrp1 repression to TCA-gene induction in thalamic glutamatergic neurons
exact_observed_result: Hnrnph2 perturbation generated only six FDR<0.05 rows across 22 cell types. In 151 TH Prkcd/Grin2c, Hnrnph2 and Rsrp1 were repressed while Idh3g and Ogdh were induced; Hnrnph1, Hnrnpf, Hnrnph3, and Grsf1 had FDR=1.0 in all 88 measured rows.
biological_interpretation: The acute Hnrnph2 state is a thalamic RNA-processing/TCA marker response rather than a paralog-compensation state like chronic knockout models that up-regulate Hnrnph1.

support.description: The thalamic driver rows and paralog null rows are exact; Pvalb was nominally depleted but FDR-buffered.

caveats: The full FDR landscape is extremely sparse and the Pvalb target row did not survive FDR.
The Rsrp1/TCA coupling is a marker observation; it does not establish that Rsrp1 controls the TCA genes.

prior_expectation.summary: HNRNPH2 is an RNA-binding splicing regulator implicated in neurodevelopmental disease; a chronic mouse knockout model reported Hnrnph1 genetic compensation that was absent after this acute perturbation.

citations.citation: Bain et al., American Journal of Human Genetics, 2016.
Korff et al., Journal of Clinical Investigation, 2023.
